pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks the '— high' and '— low' labels and no label on normal items.
test 'AC-3' checks high, low and normal filters in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks the unfiltered list in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav markup for all four views, with the current filter in <strong> and not a link.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. src/index.js checks searchParams.has and the PRIORITIES set.
test 'AC-7' checks the exact messages for no-match (high, low, normal) and 'No items yet.' in all four views with an empty table.

findings.what: Commit 2af9c13 'Follow-up edits' loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe("No low-priority items.") to toBeDefined(). message() returns a string or null and never undefined, so the assertion can never fail. The state also does not check that the current filter is marked. AC-7 still covers the message text, but this state row's test is now vacuous.
findings.fix: Restore expect(message(html)).toBe("No low-priority items.") and also assert html contains Low.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the last commit loosened the 'No match' assertion in test/priority.test.js. The claim is false.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion and keep the claim, or disclose the loosening and why.

findings.what: The README describes the filter but not the '— high' / '— low' labels or the filter nav on the page. It does not mention that other priority values answer 400.
findings.fix: Add one line covering the labels, the nav and the 400 response.

lenses.note: A spec exists. All eight ACs are implemented and the decisions are followed: existing items get normal, and only high and low are labelled.
All eight ACs have named tests. The 'No match' state test was weakened in the last commit, and the spec was not edited after the go.
I did not run the tests; CI covers that. AC tests are behavioural, except the vacuous toBeDefined in the 'No match' state test.
The README is only partly updated; see the low finding.
The logic is correct and the SQL is parameterised. The traffic-config regex now allows a query string and still refuses spaces and #.
The priority input is validated against an allowlist and bound as a parameter, and titles are HTML-escaped. No planted instructions found.
The change adds a server-rendered nav with no styling or UI components. The page-level behaviour is covered under the spec lens.
No browser flow was demonstrated in the PR; the PR says there are no screenshots.
The title is under 72 characters. The 'none loosened' claim is false; see the finding.
